title: Articles and Gender
summary: Learn masculine and feminine nouns and how articles agree with them.

sections.heading: Definite and indefinite articles
sections.body:
Portuguese nouns have gender: masculine or feminine. Articles must agree in gender and number.

| Meaning | Masculine | Feminine |
|---|---|---|
| the | **o** | **a** |
| a/an | **um** | **uma** |
| the (plural) | **os** | **as** |
| some | **uns** | **umas** |

sections.heading: Common gender patterns
sections.body: Many nouns ending in **-o** are masculine and many ending in **-a** are feminine, but there are exceptions. Learn nouns together with their article.

sections.heading: Agreement with adjectives
sections.body: Adjectives usually change to match the noun. Masculine often ends in **-o**, feminine in **-a**; plural adds **-s**.

keyPoints: Articles agree with gender and number: o/a/os/as, um/uma/uns/umas.
Learn every noun with its article because exceptions are common.
Adjectives usually agree with the noun they describe.
Words ending in -ção are usually feminine: a informação, a estação.

commonMistakes.note: Livro is masculine, so use um and novo.
